name: Gas engines
principle: Spark-ignited or dual-fuel reciprocating engines in the 1 to 20 MW class generate power from natural gas or biogas. Wärtsilä's 50SG makes about 18.4 MW at 50.2% electrical efficiency, connects to the grid within 30 seconds and reaches full load in under 2 minutes in a fast start.
key_equipment: generator circuit breaker and MV switchgear

suppliers.name: JEREH
suppliers.product: INNIO Jenbacher/Waukesha authorized integrator; 3 kVA-3,300 kVA gas gensets and distributed energy (Jereh Distributed Energy)

reference_plants.name: PLTD Pesanggaran, Bali (PT Indonesia Power)
reference_plants.status: in operation; delivered 2015 and began on HFO, primarily LNG since July 2016 (largest engine-based power plant in Indonesia)

costs.metric: total installed cost, gas engine in grid-interconnected CHP application
costs.basis: Total plant cost by baseload capacity: 100 kW $2,900; 633 kW $2,837; 1,121 kW $2,366; 3,326 kW $1,801; 9,341 kW $1,433. Covers gen-set, heat recovery (exhaust economiser, jacket-coolant HX, pump, controls, piping), interconnection/paralleling, exhaust treatment, labour and materials, engineering, project management, 5% contingency and project financing. Compiled by ICF from vendor data.

source.note: US EPA CHP Partnership, Catalog of CHP Technologies, Section 2 (reciprocating engines), Table 2-4 total installed cost, read 2026-11-16

costs.metric: total installed cost, reciprocating engine CHP
costs.basis: DOE fact sheet by size: 35 kW $4,250; 100 kW $3,700; 250 kW $3,450; 500 kW $3,150; 1 MW $2,800; 2 MW $2,550; 3 MW $2,350; 4.5 MW $2,000. Independent of the EPA table and higher at the small end (100 kW: $3,700 in 2020$ vs $2,900 in 2013$) — use as a budget range, not a market price.
